summary: Can nums1 be turned into an array of all odd or all even values, where each element is kept or replaced by nums1[i] - nums1[j] (>= 1, j != i)?
mainInsight: Subtracting an odd number flips parity, subtracting an even keeps it. If all elements already share a parity the answer is true. Otherwise odd and even elements are both present. All-even is impossible because the smallest odd element can never be changed. All-odd works iff every even element has a smaller odd element: i.e. the smallest odd is smaller than the smallest even.
canonicalApproach: Compare smallest odd and smallest even

approaches.name: Try both parities with brute force
approaches.summary: Check each element against all others.

approaches.name: Compare smallest odd and smallest even
approaches.summary: If both parities exist, return min_odd < min_even.

commonMistakes: Forgetting that all-same-parity arrays are already valid

options: Subtracting an odd value flips the parity; an even value keeps it

cards.answer: Subtracting an odd value flips the parity; an even value keeps it
cards.explanation: odd - odd = even, even - odd = odd.

incorrectOptionExplanations.Parity depends only on the larger of the: It depends on the subtracted value.

promptVariants: Why is 'all odd' feasible iff the smallest odd is smaller than the smallest even (when both exist)?
cards.answer: Each even element e must be replaced by e - o for some odd o < e (to become odd); that exists for every even iff the smallest odd is below the smallest even. Making all even is impossible because the smallest odd number would need to subtract a smaller odd number, which does not exist. Odd numbers are unchanged for the all-odd target.
keyPoints: Smallest odd cannot be fixed for all-even
cards.explanation: If all numbers share a parity, return true immediately.
